## The problem

AMCB's public directory publishes **22,309 certificants** -- name, credential,
status, dates.

It publishes **no address at any level.** Not state, not ZIP, not county.

> Every geographic statement about this workforce -- where midwives are, where
> they're leaving, who they're near -- has to be *derived*. There is nothing
> to look up.

**Getting even the roster out was its own problem:**

- AMCB's directory **hard-caps every search at 500 rows** -- paging past row
  500 fails outright. Worked around by partitioning certification numbers into
  digit-by-digit buckets that each stay under the cap, then summing the exact
  `Total : N` line per bucket
- **No bulk export, no API** -- only an Oracle APEX HTML report with
  server-side session state that drops and must be reconnected mid-scrape
- **No location data published anywhere.** City/state sit behind AMCB's paid,
  per-record primary-source verification -- deliberately never purchased or
  scraped; nothing here comes from behind a paywall or a login
- The **NPI Registry API caps responses at 200 rows per query** too, and
  returns them alphabetically (not by relevance) -- paged past that cap up to
  its 1,200-row hard ceiling, or candidates for common names (e.g. "Smith,
  John") silently go missing

## AMCB's publicly searchable database

```{r fig-amcb-screenshot}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, "docs", "figures",
  "amcb_instant_verification_screenshot.png"))
```

AMCB's "Instant Verification" tool (`ams.amcbmidwife.org`) is searchable by
name or certification number and returns **status only** -- Active, Retired,
Deceased, Lapsed, Suspended, and so on. No practice address, city, state or
ZIP appears anywhere on it, and AMCB itself states it is "not considered
primary source." This is the entire public roster this project starts from.

## What we built

A reproducible pipeline that turns an unlocated certification roster into a
located, auditable cohort, plus the analyses and manuscript built on top of
it:

1. **Scrape** the AMCB directory (name, credential, status)
2. **Link** each certificant to an NPI (National Provider Identifier)
3. **Geocode** the linked practice address -> county, ACOG district, rurality
4. **Enrich** with CMS, Trilliant claims, Healthgrades, CABC birth-center data
5. **Characterize** the located cohort (Table 1)
6. **Track** the 2007-2025 provider panel for entry, movement, and attrition
7. **Write it up** -- a manuscript, 4 tables, 7 figures, 3 appendices

## Data sources

| Source | What it gives us |
|---|---|
| AMCB public directory | the roster itself: name, credential, status, dates |
| NPI Registry (NPPES) | identity link, practice address, 2007-2025 panel |
| CMS Doctors & Clinicians | hospital affiliation, school, sex, age |
| Trilliant provider directory | backup sex/school/age, patient-panel mix |
| Healthgrades | profile attributes, language (partial) |
| CABC | birth-center accreditation |
| USDA RUCC, ACS, CDC WONDER | rurality, population denominators, births |

## Table 1, variable by variable: where it actually comes from

| Variable | Primary source | Backup / fallback | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certification, status, dates | AMCB directory (`ams.amcbmidwife.org`) | -- | 22,309 on the roster; cohort is 12,052 CNM (99.0%) + 119 CM (1.0%) of 12,171 ACTIVE, primary-linked |
| Sex | NPPES (self-enumerated) | Trilliant | 12,089 female (`r mw_safe_stat("table1.female_pct", "%.1f")`%), 65 male (0.5%), 17 not recorded |
| Training institution | CMS DAC, cleaned by `strip_med_suffix()` | Healthgrades -> repository -> Trilliant (last; agrees with DAC on every overlap) | DAC alone names a school for only 14.3% of the cohort; Trilliant's DAC-derived string reaches ~400 more (678 overlap, 100% agree); built, not yet in the published Table 1 |
| Years observed / age-in-panel | NPPES panel itself | NBER's mirror of NPPES for pre-2024 snapshots | <5 yrs 2,597 (21.3%), 5-9 yrs 2,885 (23.7%), 10-14 yrs 2,424 (19.9%), >=15 yrs 4,265 (35%) |
| Clinician age | OH voter DOBs (3-tier disambiguated against 7.95M records), WA DOH direct birth years, Healthgrades ages -- N=5,448 ground-truth, 100% verified | Ordinary least squares: Age = 35.86 + 0.943 x years-certified (R^2=0.72, residual error ~7.4 yrs), fitted on the 5,448 and applied to impute every one of the other 16,861 roster members | built (Technical Appendix, `artifacts/amcb_calibrated_ages.csv`); not yet in the published Table 1 |
| Median patient-panel age | Trilliant claims | -- | median (IQR) 32 (30-35) yrs across 10,877 midwives with an observed panel (89.4% of cohort); no other source has this at all |
| Practice address | NPPES (self-enumerated) | NPPES secondary (pl_pfile), CMS DAC facility, Trilliant claims site | switching pl_pfile vintage alone lifted cohort secondary locations from 2,687 to 5,303 -- see "The work-site address problem" |
| Hospital affiliation | CMS DAC (Tier 1, Medicare enrollment) | Tier 2 municipal co-location (sensitivity), Trilliant claims -> hospital CCN | Table 1: 7,685 (64.4%) have >=1 observed hospital site; Tier-2 recall vs. Tier-1 is 50.59% (903/1,785); negative control: 0 structural NPI Type-1<->Type-2 matches |
| ACOG district, rurality (RUCC) | Geocoded practice address | USDA RUCC 2023 / ACOG boundaries | metro 10,831 (90.4%), nonmetro-adjacent 800 (6.7%), nonmetro-remote 344 (2.9%); 196 unresolved |
| Primary claims-site setting | Trilliant claims | CMS DAC facility affiliation, CABC | hospital 6,527 (64.3%), clinic/practice 2,605 (25.7%), FQHC 651 (6.4%), birth center 169 (1.7%) |
| Language | Healthgrades | -- | currently unavailable: not collected by NPPES, CMS DAC, or the Healthgrades scrape |
| Accepts new patients, telehealth | Healthgrades | -- | currently unavailable: Healthgrades data not available for this cohort |

## Linking a name to a person

A same-surname candidate pool means a perfect name match can still be the
**wrong person.** So identity is *ranked*, not scored:

- Candidates come from a **surname block** -- the NPI Registry query itself
- Ranked into a **name-evidence class**: exact full name, then first+last,
  then last name + first initial, then nickname- and former/maiden-name
  expansion
- Narrowed by **credential/taxonomy compatibility** -- an NPI credentialed MD
  or DO is rejected as almost certainly a different person who shares the name
- A record resolves only when exactly **one** candidate occupies the
  strongest class it reaches; everything else is **quarantined**, not
  discarded

**Deliberately not used:**

- **Gender** -- the cohort is ~99% women, so gender blocking discriminates
  poorly and would have to be *inferred* from first name: risk without benefit
- **Age** -- built (`validate_age_at_certification.R`) but not active; it
  needs a year-of-birth the current AMCB scrape doesn't provide

`r mw_safe_stat("linkage.matched_pct", "%.1f")`% of the roster links to a

mostly-active subset -- stated, not implied.

## Table 1: who the cohort is

Built from the frozen linkage plus every enrichment layer, with one rule: a
block that cannot resolve a denominator shows its unresolved rows rather than
dropping them.

- `r mw_safe_stat("table1.cnm_pct", "%.1f")`% Certified Nurse-Midwife /
  `r mw_safe_stat("table1.cm_pct", "%.1f")`% Certified Midwife
- `r mw_safe_stat("table1.female_pct", "%.1f")`% female
- Median patient-panel age (Trilliant claims): 32 years (IQR 30-35)
- `r mw_safe_stat("cohort.metro_pct", "%.1f")`% practice in a metropolitan
  county

Full table: `docs/table1_midwives.md` / `artifacts/table1_midwives.csv`.

## The persistence question

Retention is proposed as a way to sustain midwife-led obstetric access. That
carries an assumption nobody had measured: **is a midwife retained in the
profession retained in the same community?**

- `r mw_safe_stat("panel.year_min")`-`r mw_safe_stat("panel.year_max")`
  NPPES practice-location panel, one row per provider per year
- Three observable quantities: **entry**, **county-to-county movement**,
  **cessation**
- Tracked against rurality strata and state scope-of-practice regime, not
  just in aggregate

## What we found: persistence is sticky year-to-year, not over a career

```{r fig-rural}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
r <- K$rural$table
r$origin <- factor(r$origin, levels = rev(r$origin))

ggplot(r, aes(x = pct, y = origin)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0.10, linewidth = 0.5,
                 color = "grey35") +
  geom_point(size = 3.4, color = "grey15") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)), vjust = -1.6, size = 4.2,
            color = "grey15") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(55, 71), breaks = seq(55, 70, 5),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Ended career in county of first practice", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.margin = margin(6, 14, 6, 6))
```

Annual same-county persistence: `r mw_safe_stat("persist.annual_county", "%.1f")`%.
Career-long: `r mw_safe_stat("persist.career_county", "%.1f")`%. Metropolitan
minus remote: `r mw_safe_stat("rural.diff", "%.1f")` percentage points.

## Where movers go

```{r fig-movers}
m <- K$movers$table
d <- data.frame(
  origin = rep(rownames(m), times = ncol(m)),
  dest   = rep(colnames(m), each = nrow(m)),
  n      = as.vector(m))
d$origin <- factor(d$origin, levels = rev(rownames(m)))
d$dest   <- factor(d$dest, levels = colnames(m))
d$pct    <- 100 * d$n / ave(d$n, d$origin, FUN = sum)

ggplot(d, aes(x = pct, y = origin, fill = dest)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62, color = "white", linewidth = 0.7,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(pct >= 7, sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), ""), color = dest),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), size = 3.8,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("To metropolitan"      = "grey30",
                               "To nonmetro adjacent" = "grey65",
                               "To nonmetro remote"   = "grey86"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("To metropolitan"      = "white",
                                "To nonmetro adjacent" = "grey15",
                                "To nonmetro remote"   = "grey15")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Percentage of movers from that origin", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.size = unit(0.45, "cm"),
        plot.margin = margin(6, 14, 6, 6))
```

Rural-origin movers relocate predominantly to metropolitan counties -- supply
can thin in a county without the national count changing at all.

## What makes this reproducible

- **Every artifact carries a provenance sidecar** -- SHA-256 of each input, so
  any figure traces to the run that produced it
- **Absence is never zero.** Suppressed cells, unobserved activity, and
  unascertained attributes stay `NA`
- **The manuscript's statistics catalog is rebuilt on every render**, never
  cached -- a stale input moves the number, it doesn't get frozen
- **Identity evidence is ranked, never scored** -- a tie is a tie, not an
  average

## Honest limits

- **Scope is CNM/CM only.** Certified Professional Midwives and
  state-licensed direct-entry midwives are outside the AMCB directory
  entirely -- this understates midwifery access, worst where non-AMCB
  midwifery is strongest
- **The linked subset is not a random sample** of the roster
- Employer/organization affiliation is built but **withheld** -- its linkage
  agreement (16.4%) falls below the accepted threshold
- Practice setting is built but **not yet in Table 1** -- an unruled decision
- Birth-attendance via Medicare claims was **retracted**: public Medicare Part
  B carries no delivery-code rows for any provider, 2013-2023
